brief.text:
The fork to pick before the full set is drawn.

Every written stream — a contact's Conversation and Full-timers, an interaction's thread, the Around card, DMs, groups, announcements — moves to one Slack-style grammar: oldest at top, composer pinned at the foot, author grouping, day dividers, everything left-aligned, replies one level deep in a Thread pane.

What is still open is density: how much container a message gets. Each row draws the same two moments in one direction:

• the contact's Conversation in the real 460px drawer at the reported 1107×662 laptop — viewer Maria, a Full-timer;
• the Everyone on Campus announcement channel at 1440 with its Thread open beside — viewer Josh, a Trainee.

The composer is identical in every row on purpose, so only the stream varies. Sample people; no real record is depicted.

noteA.text:
A · No containers. 36px avatar, name and time on one line, body beneath; a second message from the same author within a few minutes drops its avatar. The row lights on hover and grows a toolbar (Josh's row shows it).

Most messages per screen — in the 460px drawer you read five exchanges before the composer. Asks and questions are told apart only by a tag and a status line, so they can be scrolled past.

An announcement is a row like any other; the New line and the pin strip carry what the card used to.

noteB.text:
B · Every message, or run of messages from one author, sits in a #F4F4F5 card — the shipped announcement .post, generalised.

Each card is unmistakably one thing, and actions have an obvious home in the card foot. The cost is density: the same drawer shows about three cards. A plain "Yeah, I'll sit with him" gets as much frame as a follow-up ask.

The Thread pane is cards too, so a reply looks exactly like a post.

noteC.text:
C · Rows by default; a card only where the message is a thing with state — a follow-up ask, a question, an announcement post.

Chatter stays dense, and the messages someone has to act on stand out of it without a colour. The rule is learnable: a card means "this wants something from someone".

In the Thread pane the announcement is a card and its replies are rows, which reads as "the post, and people talking about it".

noteK.text:
Independent of density: where does an ask say it is an ask?

1 · A tag beside the name, and a status line under the body.
2 · A rule in the gutter, coloured by kind, with the status line.
3 · No tag — the status line alone names it.

Each column shows the same four messages: an open ask seen by its asker (both buttons), an ask someone followed up, an ask its asker withdrew, and a question. A question carries no state in the model today, so it has only its label.

The buttons are the real verbs from CONTEXT.md: I followed up, Never mind.

titleA.text: A · picked — its boards lead the Full set page

titleC.text: C · Rows, with cards for announcements and asks

wBrief.text:
Direction A (Slack-literal rows) with the kind as a tag beside the name — picked 2026-09-29. ADR 0033.

Every board is drawn in the one grammar: 36px avatar, name and time on a line, body beneath; the same author within a few minutes drops the avatar; left-aligned throughout; hover toolbar; day dividers and a New line; oldest at top with the composer pinned.

A Thread opens beside the stream where there is width (Messages at 1440) and replaces it, with a back arrow, where there isn't (the 460px drawer, an Around card).

wN1.text:
Full-timers: the lock and "Trainees can't" sit in the header, because the header is the only thing that tells a Full-timer which of the two streams a Trainee reads. The composer has no kind chips — asks belong on the Conversation.

Copy change: "Add to the Full-timers thread…" becomes "Write something only Full-timers will see…" — thread now means replies to one message only.

Interaction threads stay on the log entry (Q8a): the story row carries a replies chip and the drawer opens on the interaction quoted as the parent.

wN2.text:
Around keeps its rules (ADR 0022): one card open, reading in place, Conversation and Full-timers as a segment, the composer posting into the open one and naming its audience, the just-posted message landing above the composer.

Inside a card avatars step down to 28px — the only size change in the grammar. "I followed up" works right on the card; there is no Never mind here because the viewer is not the asker.

wN3.text:
Messages: DMs and groups lose mine-on-the-right. Josh's own message is a row like Ruth's.

The poster's view shows "Read by 21 of 24 · 17 said got it" as one link to the receipts; a member sees Got it. The audience line above the composer replaces the hardcoded "Posting to everyone on Campus" (#1243).

The pin strip names who pinned and what unpinning does; the pinned post stays first.

wN4.text:
The composer is one box everywhere. Kind chips live inside it on a Conversation only; the audience line sits above it on every contact stream.

Your notes: Follow-ups become rows in the same grammar — the team posts as "The team", your own can be edited, and the public-tracker line stays under the box because every Follow-up is mirrored to GitHub.

Mobile at 390 is not drawn yet — two questions about the person screen are open.

mN.text:
The same grammar at 390, every target 44px.

The person screen's "Alongside" tab becomes Conversation (Q21a). It used to merge the Conversation, every interaction's thread and — for a Full-timer — the staff-only Full-timers messages into one unmarked list. A Full-timer now gets the same Conversation / Full-timers switch the Around card uses; a Trainee never sees the switch.

Interaction threads move to their Story entry (Q22): a replies chip, or "Think it through together" when there are none, opening a pushed Thread.

A Thread is a pushed screen with back. Long-press stands in for the hover toolbar. Members can finally reply in an announcement's thread and say Got it on the phone — neither exists in the app today.
